jobs.title: Water Resources Project Manager
jobs.description:
Communities everywhere share the need for clean water. And as they work to meet that need, they’re facing new, more complex challenges every day. Our water professionals collaborate to contribute innovative ideas, guided by scientific rigor and a vision for sustainable growth. Every day, we’re helping communities improve, reuse, and protect our world’s most precious resource.

Join our team to deliver transformational projects that will benefit future generations. Grow with us, H2O+U.

Stantec is seeking an experienced Project/Program Manager to join our inter-disciplinary team as a Water Resources Project/Program Manager. You will be an integral part of the leadership team, working closely with regional leadership in advancing a growing water resources project portfolio while building a robust community of practice around the integration of technical, environmental, economic, and social considerations regarding water resources. This role will enable you to apply and grow your expertise in water resources planning and management to support policy and program development, decision-making, and project implementation to help our clients address complex water resource management challenges.

We're looking for professionals with deep experience building and running large water resources projects and programs in the western US. Our Water Resources team tackles challenges in California and throughout the West that address water availability and quality, changing water demands, climate vulnerability and risk, environmental protection and enhancement, and the institutional, legislative, and financial frameworks that shape water management. Your role will include leading a growing team, managing large and complex water resource planning projects, developing and maintaining client relationships, mentoring staff and advancing a collaborative environment of knowledge sharing, and contributing technically at the interface of policy, management, science and engineering.

Your Key Responsibilities

The following outlines key performance aspects and responsibilities that we anticipate with your role. These responsibilities and expectations are organized according to the four pillars of our business: managing our business and staff, doing work, winning work, and innovating.

MANAGE – Project Management

Serve as project manager for water resources projects with accountability for scope, schedule, budget, and quality performance, from both client and Stantec perspectives.
Effectively lead, challenge, and inspire staff; structure work assignments and delegation to expand delivery capacity, including creating opportunities for junior technical resources on projects under contract.
Mentor and coach developing professionals through project assignments, exposure to different levels of responsibility, and interaction with clients and stakeholders.
Coordinate with Stantec leadership routinely on budget planning, workload forecasting, and staff resourcing needs.

DO – Project Work

Provide project leadership for water resources planning and management engagements in the Pacific Region and West, performing a variety of tasks to plan, execute and deliver water resources planning and management services.
Apply your knowledge of, and experience in Western water policy, water resources planning, and project implementation to lead project team and deliver multi-objective water resources programs involving agricultural, municipal and industrial, and environmental water uses, hydropower, flood risk management, and other purposes.
Advise and support state agencies, Tribes, irrigation and water districts, municipalities, and non-governmental clients on water resources programs, funding strategy, and financial assistance administration, including water supply development, water efficiency, water reuse, and related program areas.
Remain current on state and federal legislation, appropriations/budgets, agency policy, and regulations affecting Pacific and western water programs, and translate developments into practical guidance for clients and project teams.

WIN – Business Development

Identify trends and leverage your knowledge of the water industry, water market and clients to guide pursuit strategies with federal, state, regional and private clients.
Engage our clients in meaningful discussions about their most critical issues and translate those discussions into opportunities to deliver solutions.
Develop and deepen client relationships over time through high-quality delivery and thought leadership.
Prepare proposals, provide strategic insight and lead aspects of marketing efforts.
Enhance Stantec's brand presence and reputation in the industry through active participation in professional associations, conferences, and publications.

INNOVATE – Technical Growth and Innovation

Develop and deploy scalable program delivery tools to communicate program performance and project-specific information to clients, funders, and the public.
Collaborate with Stantec's Office of Growth/Innovation to support global knowledge sharing groups that foster and grow innovative ideas to address water resource management challenges.
Develop innovative program and funding solutions to address regulatory drivers, aging infrastructure, cost efficiency, and other market drivers.

Your Capabilities and Credentials

Leadership

Skilled leader and collaborative team player capable of building relationships both internally and externally.
Skilled communicator in both oral and written communications, including briefings to executives, governing bodies, and public audiences.
Skilled at building consensus and cooperation with staff, clients, and stakeholders at all experience levels.
Skilled at inspiring, motivating, and holding teams accountable for delivery of complex, multi-project programs.

Technical Expertise

Recognized industry leadership in the development, implementation, and management of large-scale water resources projects and programs in the western US.
Experience and expertise with policy, technical analysis, and integration of diverse expertise to support water resource planning and management projects.
Experience with Federal and State legislative processes, budget development, and policy analysis affecting water resources programs.
Experience in managing staff, prioritizing activities, and assigning tasks to meet project targets, budgets, and deliverables, including supervisory, hiring, and performance management responsibilities.
Experience building and maintaining productive working relationships with state agencies, Tribes, irrigation and water districts, local governments, and non-governmental organizations.

Education and Experience

Bachelor's degree in public policy, engineering, science, hydrology, or a related field required; advanced degree in a related field preferred.
Proven subject expertise; typically, 10 or more years of experience in water resources planning and management, including supervisory, management, and fiscal responsibilities.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills for working in diverse team environments with staff, clients, and stakeholders.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee and other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

About The Role

What if your expertise in climate modeling, ecology, or sustainability could directly shape how AI understands and reasons about the world's most urgent environmental challenges? We're looking for Environmental Science experts — Masters and PhD holders — to help build and train cutting-edge AI models by developing rigorous, real-world scientific problems that push the boundaries of machine reasoning.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role designed for working scientists and researchers who want to apply their domain expertise in a new and impactful way. Full training support is provided — no prior AI experience needed.

Deep expertise in one or more areas: climate modeling, ecology, sustainability, environmental policy, or earth systems science

Department Information

California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) brings together the state’s recycling and waste management programs to move the state towards a circular economy that reduces waste and reuses all materials.

Through landmark initiatives like the Integrated Waste Management Act and Beverage Container Recycling and Litter Reduction Act, California works toward a society that uses less, recycles more, and takes resource conservation to higher and higher levels.

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations t hrough the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. Together we further our mission to protect the environment and preserve resources by empowering Californians to reduce, reuse, and recycle. Join CalRecycle to improve the lives of all Californians.

Department Website: http://www.calrecycle.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

Do you have a passion to perform a variety of scientific, analytical, and technical assistance duties to implement enforcement requirements and assist with program analysis of compliance policies for CalRecycle’s Responsible Textile Recovery Act of 2024? Do you enjoy working in a collaborative, dynamic environment? CalRecycle is seeking an enthusiastic Environmental Scientist to join our talented team that is passionate to work in Textiles Unit!

Position Description

Under the direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist (incumbent) at Range A (an entry level employee) works under direct supervision performing the least complex scientific work; at Range B (an intermediate level employee) works under general supervision performing moderately complex work; or at Range C (a journey person level employee) works independently performing the most complex work. The Environmental Scientist (ES) will have a variety of responsibilities from scientific, analytical, and administrative duties to implement and enforce the Responsible Textile Recovery Act of 2024 within the Textiles Unit. The incumbent applies the principles of scientific research and analytical skills to perform complex technical tasks and uses statistical knowledge to gather, assess, and review data in order to ensure their compliance with CalRecycle's producer responsibility and product stewardship requirements and regulations. The incumbent is responsible for the determination of violations and their general effects on public health, safety, and the environment for the programs, reviewing findings and preparing the reports for technical adequacy on enforcement matters, and doing other related work to perform the duties listed below. Additionally, the ES will play an important role in developing and implementing new enforcement programs related to products with EPR and product stewardship requirements.

The Program is responsible for compliance and enforcement related to producer responsibility, product stewardship and seeks to enforce EPR laws governing the regulated communities including, but not limited to: Producer Responsibility Organizations (PRO), producers/manufacturers of covered products, licensees of trademarks or brands, importers, distributors, wholesalers, retailers and other regulated parties. The incumbent will determine if regulated communities are in compliance by performing field inspections and investigations. On a daily basis, conduct research of businesses, products, and industries to plan inspections and conduct investigations; develop sound conclusions and recommendations for the issuance of timely, concise and complete inspection reports; and compile defensible facts for legal documents. Serve as an EPR compliance program liaison and educate stakeholders verbally and in writing; accurately explain the law and potential enforcement consequences; prepare correspondence; meet regulatory deadlines; and implement established enforcement processes. Work in coordination with CalRecycle’s other supporting technical staff and the Legal Office; evaluate the significance of violations of non-compliant entities and program trends; compile, organize data and use mathematical formulas and develop databases and tools to perform statistical analyses to track compliance trends of the regulated community to evaluate overall program success; recommend corrective actions or penalties and fines to effectively achieve the program(s) mandates to protect public health and safety and the environment. Prepare findings to present and conduct technical trainings to supervisors, technical offices, Executive Management and Stakeholders.

This position involves traveling throughout California involving multiple, consecutive days away from the office and overnight stays. The incumbent must have a current California Driver’s License and participate in the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Employer Pull Notice Program.

As of July 1st, 2026, the position is office-centered and employees will be expected to report to the office at least four days per week.
This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.

Founded in 1866, San Jose Water Company is an investor owned water company headquartered in Silicon Valley. With a service area of 140 square miles, it is one of the largest and most technically sophisticated urban water system in the United States. We serve over 1 million people with high quality, life sustaining water, with an emphasis on exceptional customer service.

We are actively seeking talented, driven and highly-productive applicants for the position of Manager of Water Resources and Supply Strategy to join our dynamic team. We offer a challenging and rewarding work environment along with a competitive salary and an excellent benefits package.

Position Summary

Under the general direction of the Vice President of Engineering, the Manager of Water Resources and Supply Strategy
is responsible for leading the Company's water supply planning, water rights administration, and strategic water supply initiatives. The position serves as the Company's primary resource for water supply strategy, long-term resource planning, and water rights management and is responsible for advancing projects and programs that support reliable, resilient, and cost-effective water service.

The Manager leads major water supply initiatives, including potable reuse, desalination, groundwater, recycled water, imported water, and other supply diversification efforts. The position oversees consultants and technical advisors, independently evaluates water supply programs, investments, and agreements, manages water rights matters, and provides technical, operational, financial, and strategic analyses to support executive decision-making. Major duties require the frequent use of initiative, independent judgment, and collaboration with personnel within and outside the Company.

Specific Responsibilities

Leads the Company's water supply planning, resource management, water rights administration, and long-term water supply strategy activities.
Serves as the Company's lead project manager for major water supply initiatives, including potable reuse, desalination, groundwater, recycled water, imported water, and other supply diversification projects.
Directs and oversees consultants, contractors, and technical advisors engaged in water supply planning, engineering, environmental review, design, and implementation activities.
Develops and evaluates water supply plans, forecasts, project alternatives, capital investments, agreements, and resource strategies to support reliable and cost-effective service.
Conducts independent technical, operational, financial, and policy analyses of water supply programs, investments, and agreements to support prudent stewardship of customer resources and informed utility decision-making.
Monitors and evaluates regulatory, legislative, environmental, and industry developments affecting water supply reliability, water rights, and resource management.
Coordinates activities with Company departments, regulatory agencies, governmental organizations, regional water agencies, and other external stakeholders.
Represents the Company in matters related to water supply planning, resource management, strategic water supply initiatives, and regulatory proceedings as required.
Leads and coordinates multidisciplinary teams of consultants, contractors, and technical advisors and manages associated budgets, schedules, contracts, and objectives.
Performs special projects and other related duties as assigned.

Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Extensive knowledge of civil engineering principles and practices related to water resources, water supply systems, utility infrastructure, and resource management.
Knowledge of California water rights, water policy, water resource planning, and regulatory frameworks affecting water utilities.
Knowledge of project management, consultant management, contract administration, and capital project delivery.
Familiarity with potable reuse, desalination, groundwater management, recycled water, wastewater, imported water supplies, and other water supply development strategies.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex technical, operational, financial, and regulatory issues, utility economics, capital investments, and lifecycle costs.
Ability to develop and evaluate water supply strategies, resource plans, infrastructure investments, and long-term planning alternatives.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with Company personnel, consultants, regulatory agencies, governmental organizations, and other stakeholders.
Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, manage consultant performance, and effectively influence outcomes across organizational boundaries.

Required Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Civil Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline.
Minimum of eight (8) years of progressively responsible professional engineering experience related to water resources, water supply planning, utility infrastructure, capital project management, or resource management.
Minimum of five (5) years of significant project leadership experience involving complex multidisciplinary initiatives and coordination of multiple stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience managing complex projects involving multiple stakeholders, consultants, regulatory agencies, and external partners.
Experience preparing technical analyses, reports, presentations, and recommendations to support executive decision-making.
Registration as a Professional Civil Engineer in the State of California is required.
Master of Business Administration (MBA), Master's degree in Engineering, Water Resources, Public Administration, or a related field is preferred.

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the incumbent performs a broad range of scientific and professional office and field duties involving the research, environmental analysis, outreach, and logistics for the Biological Control Program and the Integrated Pest Control Branch.  

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!

### **Working Conditions**


Approximately 60% of the workload will be in permanent buildings or trailers leased or owned by the State or cooperating agencies or other locations. The setting is standard with a phone, computer, keyboard, desks, tables, chairs, fax machine, copier, stapler, printers, calculators, and writing instruments. Computer software used may include MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, and Publisher as well as other databases/software created especially for a given research task.  

The remaining 40% of the workload requires traveling to remote and/or populated areas within the State of California via government (State or Federal) vehicle (car/truck). When working in the field, the incumbent works alone or with a group of field scientists and/or seasonals. Incumbent may also be required to navigate variable lengths of distance over unpredictable terrain. Incumbent may work extended hours and days at any given time in the month including holidays. The incumbent may be required on short notice to work on emergency projects for the Branch or any other program for the Plant Division. This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. Description:
**Sustainment \& Restoration Services (SRS)** is a Native American, tribally\-owned small business. We are a full\-service, multi\-discipline environmental, engineering, construction support, munitions response, and specialized professional services company wholly\-owned by the Oneida Nation as a subsidiary under Oneida ESC Group.


Serving the federal market and civilian agencies, including US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), US Department of Defense, US Air Force, US Navy and Marine Corps, US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), US Department of Agriculture (USDA), Food and Drug Administration (FDA), US Fish and Wildlife Service, and state and local customers. We collaborate with our customers to achieve long\-term environmental stewardship goals with reduced life\-cycle program costs.


SRS has an immediate opening for a **Geologist, Engineer, or Environmental Scientist \- Junior to Mid Level** based in our **Walnut Creek office**. The successful candidate will work both in the field and the office to support various environmental remediation projects at various locations in CA and beyond. This will be an **in\-person position with some flexibility to work from home periodically**.

  



**Key Responsibilities \- Office:**

* Prepare project planning documents (work plans, quality control plans, health and safety plans, sampling, and analysis plans).
* Understand applicable permits and plans that dictate how each task shall be performed.
* Conduct fieldwork preparation (procuring subcontracts, materials and equipment, and scheduling subcontractors/vendors).
* Support environmental compliance in Wastewater, Storm Water, Groundwater, and Solid Waste programs through documentation, sample preparation result analysis.
* Compile and interpret complex technical data and prepare technical memorandums and project reports as the principal author; respond to internal, client, and regulatory comments.
* Work and communicate in a team environment to ensure quality project execution.
* Assist the Technical Lead supporting project technical and financial goals and collaborating with stakeholders to successfully meet project objectives.

**Key Responsibilities \- Field:**

* Comply with project planning documents (work plans, quality control plans, health and safety plans, sampling, and analysis plans).
* Perform soil, groundwater, sediment, wastewater, storm water sampling in accordance with applicable permits and plans.
* Perform routine facility inspections and reporting.
* Complete required field documentation.
* Coordinate with the analytical laboratory to have required bottles on\-hand and to deliver collected samples to the laboratory.
* Critically think and make sound decisions to troubleshoot issues while working in the field.


Requirements:

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Engineering, or related Environmental Science field with 3\-5 years of field environmental sampling experience, OR Master’s degree in Geology, Engineering, or related Environmental Science field and 1\-3 years of field environmental sampling experience
* Ability to gain access to Department of Defense project sites (US citizen with the ability to pass a federal background check).
* Valid driver's license with a good driving record and the ability to travel and drive regularly.
* Experience working with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
* Experience with environmental compliance under Clean Water Act (CWA), National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), Industrial Stormwater Multi\-Sector General Permit (MSGP), and Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4\) regulations.
* Strong attention to detail, with excellent analytical and problem\-solving capabilities to ensure compliance with project requirements.
* Ability to provide excellent customer service, build rapport with clients, and remain responsive to client needs and expectations.
* Possess excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to interact effectively with the project team, customers, and stakeholders.
* Demonstrated ability to follow directions and work independently, as well as in a team environment, and understand project roles and responsibilities.
* Demonstrates a high standard of quality for work products.
* Possess a positive professional attitude and be flexible when challenges arise.

  



**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience with local City of Fairfield, Solano and Yuba Counties, and CA state regulations and permit compliance, focusing on water quality.
* Knowledge of CWA, NPDES, MSGP, MS4, and other environmental regulations.
* Ability to become a registered professional (PG, PE, PMP).

* Hands\-on field experience with soil, groundwater, sediment, wastewater, and storm water sampling.

jobs.title: Water Resources Manager
jobs.description:
The San Diego County Water Authority is seeking an experienced and forward-thinking leader to oversee key technical functions central to the region’s long-term water reliability. This position is responsible for guiding both water supply planning and facility planning, ensuring that the agency’s resource strategies and infrastructure initiatives are grounded in sound engineering analysis, regulatory awareness, and long-range forecasting.

Serving as a technical program lead, the incumbent directs complex analytical work involving hydrologic modeling, water demand forecasting, system evaluations, and planning-level engineering studies. The role oversees the development of major planning documents that inform capital investments, operational strategies, and long-term resource sustainability. In addition, the position administers water supply programs, ensuring alignment with regional needs, statewide policy objectives, and evolving environmental and regulatory requirements. This includes administration of the Carlsbad Desalination Plant Water Purchase Agreement.

The Water Authority operates in a dynamic public-sector environment, and this role requires an individual who is highly engaged, collaborative, and well-versed in regional water issues. The incumbent regularly participates in industry conferences, technical committees, and regional coordination efforts to remain current on emerging trends, regulatory developments, and best practices in water management.

This position also serves as a primary technical representative to internal and external audiences. The incumbent prepares and delivers presentations to the Board of Directors, member agencies, community groups, and professional organizations, translating complex engineering, planning, and policy information into clear, actionable insights that support informed decision-making.

As a key member of the department’s leadership team, the role includes comprehensive management of staff, including supervision of technical personnel, development of annual work plans, employee development and training, and mentorship to support high-performing teams. The successful candidate will foster collaboration, continuous improvement, and technical excellence across all program areas.

Together, these responsibilities make this position essential to advancing the Water Authority’s mission of providing a safe, reliable water supply through strategic planning, sound engineering, and effective program administration.

Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in natural or physical sciences, economics, natural resources management, urban or regional planning, civil or environmental engineering, public administration, or a closely related field supplemented by ten years of increasingly responsible professional water resources experience, including two years at the level of the Water Authority's Principal Water Resources Specialist class or equivalent.

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Measurement Assessment and Research Section (MARS) operates one of the Mobile Source Emissions Testing Facilities within the Mobile Source Laboratory Division (MSLD), equipped with Portable Emissions Measurement Systems (PEMS) and Portable Emissions Acquisition Systems (PEAQS) to generate high\-quality, legally defensible emissions data. MARS’s mission is to support the development and implementation of heavy\-duty on\-road and off\-road vehicle regulations, strengthen emissions inventories, inform enforcement actions, advance the Clean Truck Check program, and support innovative emissions research. Through surveillance testing of in\-use on\-road and off\-road heavy\-duty vehicles and equipment, MARS provides critical insights into real\-world emissions performance and regulatory effectiveness. MARS also serves as a platform for evaluating and demonstrating new testing approaches, developing innovative methods for measuring in\-use emissions, and expanding CARB’s testing capabilities. In collaboration with CARB mobile source workgroups, MARS develops and executes comprehensive test plans, conducts emissions testing, and performs robust data analyses to inform policy and regulatory decisions. Collectively, these efforts provide a scientific foundation for reducing criteria pollutants, greenhouse gases, and toxic air contaminants from the heavy\-duty sector and protecting public health and air quality.  

MARS is seeking an Air Pollution Specialist to perform complex technical work related to in\-use emissions characterization of heavy\-duty (HD) on\-road and off\-road vehicles and equipment. The incumbent will perform on\-road emissions measurements with portable emissions measurement systems (PEMS) and the Portable Emissions Acquisition System (PEAQS), and ensure compliance with established test procedures, data quality objectives, and safety protocols. Duties include developing and applying analytical methods for emissions data processing, validation, and interpretation; analyzing large datasets using computational tools; designing and executing test plans; operating advanced emissions measurement systems; coordinating test resources; and preparing technical reports in support of regulatory programs, research initiatives, and emissions assessments, while working independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to support CARB’s mission to protect air quality.  

This position offers a balanced mix of laboratory, field, and office\-based work and supports CARB’s mission by advancing in\-use emissions measurement techniques and evaluating emerging heavy\-duty vehicle technologies. Job Description And Duties

The Measurement Assessment and Research Section (MARS) operates one of the Mobile Source Emissions Testing Facilities within the Mobile Source Laboratory Division (MSLD), equipped with Portable Emissions Measurement Systems (PEMS) and Portable Emissions Acquisition Systems (PEAQS) to generate high-quality, legally defensible emissions data. MARS’s mission is to support the development and implementation of heavy-duty on-road and off-road vehicle regulations, strengthen emissions inventories, inform enforcement actions, advance the Clean Truck Check program, and support innovative emissions research. Through surveillance testing of in-use on-road and off-road heavy-duty vehicles and equipment, MARS provides critical insights into real-world emissions performance and regulatory effectiveness. MARS also serves as a platform for evaluating and demonstrating new testing approaches, developing innovative methods for measuring in-use emissions, and expanding CARB’s testing capabilities. In collaboration with CARB mobile source workgroups, MARS develops and executes comprehensive test plans, conducts emissions testing, and performs robust data analyses to inform policy and regulatory decisions. Collectively, these efforts provide a scientific foundation for reducing criteria pollutants, greenhouse gases, and toxic air contaminants from the heavy-duty sector and protecting public health and air quality.

MARS is seeking an Air Pollution Specialist to perform complex technical work related to in-use emissions characterization of heavy-duty (HD) on-road and off-road vehicles and equipment. The incumbent will perform on-road emissions measurements with portable emissions measurement systems (PEMS) and the Portable Emissions Acquisition System (PEAQS), and ensure compliance with established test procedures, data quality objectives, and safety protocols. Duties include developing and applying analytical methods for emissions data processing, validation, and interpretation; analyzing large datasets using computational tools; designing and executing test plans; operating advanced emissions measurement systems; coordinating test resources; and preparing technical reports in support of regulatory programs, research initiatives, and emissions assessments, while working independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to support CARB’s mission to protect air quality.

This position offers a balanced mix of laboratory, field, and office-based work and supports CARB’s mission by advancing in-use emissions measurement techniques and evaluating emerging heavy-duty vehicle technologies. The incumbent's position may require Statewide travel up to 30% of the time for fieldwork, training or for meetings.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

As an Environment Assessment Officer at Yarra Ranges Council, you will work within the biodiversity team full of passionate colleagues delivering conservation focussed programs for the municipality. The role will focus on supporting the Statutory Planning Department with planning application referrals that propose impacts on environmental values and natural assets. You will provide technical advice to as it relates to environmental legislation, in particular the state Native Vegetation Regulations.

This is a part-time, temporary position (parental leave backfill) for 15.2 hours (2 days) per week over 12 months.

This is a Band 6 role with an hourly rate between $49.81 and $54.29 per hour, plus superannuation.

Benefits of working with us:

Support work-life balance with your choice of monthly or fortnightly rostered day off and hybrid working arrangements.
20 weeks paid primary caregiver leave (6 weeks for secondary caregivers) plus other generous leave options such as volunteer leave, family planning, study assistance and menstrual and menopause leave.
Opportunities for professional development and to take on temporary roles in other teams to grow your skills and experience.
Novated lease vehicle options.

Experience and skills we’re looking for

Experience with working in a small team environment and application of the state planning scheme and/or native vegetation regulations
The ability to convey technical information to a variety of stakeholders and work collaboratively on complex matters, within and across teams
Diploma/degree or tertiary qualification in Natural Resource Management, Statutory/Strategic Planning, Environmental Management or related field. Related fields of work experience will be considered in lieu of formal qualifications
Great organisational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate confidently with diverse customers.

**PROJECT:** Moffett Federal Airfield at Moffett Field, CA 94035 with Avports LLC

**DEPARTMENT:**Airfield Management

**Responsibility Level:**


Responsible for the development, implementation, and monitoring of Avports Safety, Environmental and Health (SEH) Programs, including the IS\-BAH (International Standard for Business Aircraft Handling) and Safety Management System (SMS) at Moffett Federal Airfield. The chief goal is to establish a safety culture that strives to protect employees/customers, the environment and business operations.


This is a full\-time benefited salaried position.

**Essential Duties:**

* Manage all Safety, Environmental and Health Programs at Moffett Federal Airfield, provides regular reports to management on program status and compliance.
* Develop, implement and monitor an employee SEH training program to ensure compliance with Company requirements, applicable Cal/OSHA, OSHA, CalEPA, NATA (National Air Transportation Association), and IS\-BAH and SMS standards.
* Manage, regularly update and review training programs, maintain accurate employee training records to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.
* Develop training materials and provides employee training as necessary for such programs as Injury Illness Prevention Plan (IIPP), Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC), Stormwater Pollution Prevention (SWPP), Hazard Communication, Building Emergency Action Plan, Hearing Protection Program, Lock Out Tag Out, Fall Protection, and other EHS programs.
* Ensures that all staff complete any mandated EHS training assigned by the company or regulatory agencies, and maintain training completion records.
* Monitors compliance with applicable regulatory EHS standards and develop, updates all program manuals, plans, SOPs, training materials as required.
* Serves as Chair of the Safety Committee and holds monthly safety committee meetings with designated staff. Responsible for keeping meeting records to track and report progress. Also serves on the Company wide Safety Committee that meets quarterly.
* Track all safety performance indicators and generate administrative reports to monitor trends, identify areas of concern, and support continuous improvement.
* Write and review job hazard analysis, job safety analysis and implement safe work practices.
* Investigates all incidents, accidents, near miss events and hazardous conditions. Conducts risk management, root cause analysis and ensures implementation of corrective actions to mitigate risks.

* Secures and maintains environmental compliance permits with pertinent regulatory agencies.
* Holds regular safety briefings with employees to promote EHS programs.

* Maintains Ramp Safety Program and enforces airport rules and regulations through the Airfield Access and Driver’s Training program.
* Oversee the Hazardous Waste Storage area and ensure regulatory agency compliance through regular inspections (i.e. labelling, containment, proper disposal, documentation, etc.).
* Creates and manages a Environmental, Health and Safety Employee Incentive Program.
* Acts as safety liaison for airfield projects with outside contractors/vendors/organizations to oversee EHS compliance.
* Provides assistance and recommendations on EHS issues to management.
* Upholds all Company and EHS procedures and policies.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

  

* Excellent communication, organizational and technical writing skills required.
* Strong Computer skills required.
* Knowledge and experience with implementing Cal/OSHA, OSHA, Cal/EPA, EPA, BAAQM regulations and training.
* Knowledge and experience in the aviation operations industry.
* Experience in developing and managing various EHS programs in an aviation work environment.

 **Licenses, Registrations and/or Certificates:**

  

* Must pass mandatory drug screenings, criminal background checks \& obtain security clearance.
* Must maintain a valid Class C motor vehicle operator’s license as issued by the State of California.
* Completion of a Professional Line Service Technician Certification within six months of hire date.
* Completion of the IS\-BAH program workshop within six months of hire date.

* Completion of ALL Cal/OSHA required training within the first 90 days of hire date.

Apply today and join the company that is Leading with Science®.

Tetra Tech is seeking a self-motivated, Entry-Level Environmental Scientist / Compliance Specialist to support and expand our landfill and air quality compliance services within the solid waste industry. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in air regulations, landfill gas systems, emissions compliance, and environmental data analysis.

In this role, you will support regulatory compliance programs by analyzing field and operational data, interpreting air quality regulations and permit requirements, preparing compliance reports, and assisting with air permitting and emissions calculations. The primary focus areas include landfill gas monitoring, Surface Emissions Monitoring (SEM), Landfill Gas-to-Energy (LFGTE) Systems, air quality permitting, and compliance with New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Pollutants (NESHAP) regulations applicable to solid waste facilities.

This position is primarily remote, with limited, as-needed travel or occasional site visits. Only those in PST or MST will be considered.
Candidates must be comfortable working independently with limited supervision while collaborating with project managers, field staff, engineers, and regulatory specialists across geographically dispersed teams.

This position is eligible for our full benefits package including but not limited to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, Disability, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Health Spending Account (HSA), My Flex Time (MFT - paid time off), 401K, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The pay range for this position is $55K-$75K annually, based on qualifications, location, and experience. Only those that attach a cover letter will be considered.
The deadline to apply is 09/3/2026.

Your Role

Review, analyze, and interpret landfill air quality and landfill gas monitoring data, including wellfield data, SEM, and air emissions datasets.
Compare monitoring and operational data against regulatory standards, permit limits, and NSPS/NESHAP criteria to assess compliance.
Prepare environmental compliance reports, including air compliance summaries, monitoring reports, deviation analyses, and regulatory submittals.
Support the development and preparation of air quality permit applications, amendments, and renewals, including emission calculations and regulatory compliance demonstrations.
Collect, manage, track, and organize large datasets related to air emissions, landfill gas, SEM results, and compliance deadlines.
Develop and maintain templates, trackers, and tools to support consistent, accurate, and timely reporting for multiple facilities / landfills.
Coordinate with on-site operations, technicians, and subcontractors to confirm that monitoring, testing, and system performance meet regulatory and permit requirements.
Support Project Managers with deliverables, schedules, and client coordination including procurement of supplies, subcontractor coordination and Work Order development.
Contribute to multidisciplinary teams on engineering, permitting, and environmental projects.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including technical and regulatory writing.
Proficiency in MS Office – specifically Word and Excel.
Ability to work independently in a remote environment, demonstrate initiative, and manage multiple priorities with limited supervision.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with field staff, engineers, and regulatory agencies.
Valid driver’s license.
Ability and willingness to perform limited travel as required.
Interest and ability in developing technical and leadership skills within the Environmental Compliance field.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 25,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Department Fish and Wildlife's Northern Region Inland Fisheries and Wild Trout unit has an opening for a Limited Term Environmental Scientist. The incumbent will be part of a team of scientists working to survey high elevation aquatic habitats across California's northern nine counties and conduct restoration activities within the Trinity Alps Wilderness, Russian Wilderness and Marble Mountain Wilderness areas. This project seeks to reduce the compounding effects from drought, climate change, and invasive predators on declining native amphibians by identifying and actively managing invasive fish populations in key drought\-resilient lake basins and restoring sensitive amphibians to suitable habitats within their historic range.
  

  

We are seeking a highly motivated individual to join our team in a position that provides development of expertise in fisheries and herpetology science and management, survey and study design, designing, implementing, and monitoring habitat restoration projects, data analysis utilizing statistical methods, and scientific writing. This position requires indoor work at an office location and outdoor work in remote environments.

### **Job Description and Duties**


Under the direction of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will support the Department's Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture. As part of a team, the incumbent will contribute to surveys to detect, locate, and trap nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the state. Duties include: Under the supervision of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as one of the lead field scientists for the Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position will play a critical role in the coordination of field crews conducting nutria surveys and trapping across the northern portion of the nutria infestation. The incumbent will assist the Operations Supervisor with training, leading, and evaluating field crew technicians and scientific aides to survey for, detect, and remove nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the State of California. The incumbent will lead the team by example in conducting habitat suitability assessments, visual observation and camera surveys, trapping, and electronic data collection (i.e., ESRI Collector smartphone application), as well as effective use of baits and lures and obtaining entry permits from local landowners. The incumbent is responsible for conducting morning briefings of the assigned crew, tracking daily spatial assignments, and ensuring field staff understand understand project protocols. The incumbent will work with the Operations Supervisors, other field crew leads, and Planning Specialist to evaluate and help refine detection and trapping methods and tools for the most effective and efficient detection and removal of nutria. The incumbent will also closely coordinate with other regions and Department functions, as well as other affected and involved local, State, and Federal agencies. Work includes preparing draft reports and correspondence and answering routine questions from the public relative to Departmental nutria efforts. The primary geographical focus of this position will be in San Joaquin, Sacramento, Contra Costa, Solano, Alameda, and Calaveras counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture from the devastation nutria have caused in other regions of North America. Incumbent must be willing and able to competently use firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel.  

  

  



**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

Be willing to work atypical hours and on weekends. Some overnight travel (\<5%) may be required. Able to swim, walk through deep mud and thick vegetation, work on steep or uneven terrain, in extreme weather and under physically challenging conditions. Be willing and able to competently use pellet pistols or firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel. Willing to handle live animals and carcasses, dispatch animals, and conduct simple tissue sampling and necropsies. Possess valid Driver's License and be able to safely and effectively operate watercraft and Utility Task Vehicles (UTV)s, as well as tow trailers. This job requires daily operation of State vehicles to reach field sites, regular use of kayaks, and occasional operation of UTVs and motorized watercraft. Must wear Department uniform.  

  

Be willing and able to obtain a California Boater Card and other motorboat operator certifications as determined necessary.  

  

The primary geographical focus of this position will be in San Joaquin, Sacramento, Contra Costa, Solano, Alameda, and Calaveras counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation.

We are looking for someone with interest in providing quality technical field and documentation support and partnering closely with our clients. The position will be based in Los Angeles, CA.

The ideal candidate will be expected to:

Utilize their skills and experience to contribute to programmatic compliance projects.
Lead and perform field and desktop tasks (technical and non-technical) and independent analysis.
Provide technical quality oversight related to AST and USTs.
Develop accurate and complete documentation to support facility compliance.
Support with other environmental tasks, as requested.

Consulting / permitting / regulatory compliance experience in California, particularly with local CUPA agencies, SCAQMD, CARB, and Water Board.

Working knowledge of Fire Code, NFPA, APSA, STI as it applies to fuel tanks.

Oversight of tank subconsultants regarding installation, modification, removal, operation, testing, and inspection.

Organizational skills to ensure proper consulting of priorities to clients.

*The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality strives to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable environment that embraces and values diversity. **Are you passionate about preserving, enhancing, and protecting Oregon’s environment?** If so, please consider a career with the State of Oregon at the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ). At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission\-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.


The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has a full\-time opportunity available for a **Drinking Water Protection Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3\)**. This position will be located in Portland, Oregon.


This is limited duration through June 30, 2027 with the potential of being extended and/or made permanent pending Budget and Legislature approval.


Please consider joining an innovative team, and work to advance our agency’s mission to protect and improve Oregon’s environmental quality.

**About DEQ!**


The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality is the primary regulatory agency of the government of the U.S. State of Oregon responsible for protecting and enhancing the state's natural resources.


The Water Quality Division has a critical role in achieving the Department’s mission by developing policy, implementation tools, and implementation priorities for improving and protecting the quality of water in Oregon’s waterways. The Water Quality Division works cooperatively with the Department’s three regional offices and the Laboratory to deliver programs and services that protect and enhance the quality of the waters of the state to protect public health and the environment.


The Standards, Source\-water Protection, and Assessment Section is responsible for the implementation of DEQ’s Drinking Water Protection Program for source water protection. The Section is also responsible for development and adoption by rule of water quality standards, identification of outstanding resource waters and water quality limited waters, conducting a statewide water quality assessment and assembling a biennial status report on Oregon’s water quality, and providing scientific and technical assistance to the regions, laboratory, and other water quality program sections on water quality standards.


For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

**What you will do!**


You will work with DEQ and Oregon Health Authority staff in partnership to develop strategies under authority of the Clean Water Act to meet the goals and objectives of the 1996 Safe Drinking Water Act for drinking water source protection. In addition, you will provide outreach and technical assistance to Oregon’s public drinking water systems to identify sources of contamination and reduce pollution risks to their drinking water source areas.

**What’s in it for you!**


The opportunity to work in a productive and creative environment where no two days are ever the same! DEQ cares deeply about employee wellness and benefits. We offer a competitive benefits package that offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for the employee and their qualified family members, as well as paid sick leave, vacation leave, personal leave, and 11 paid holidays a year. In addition, we offer membership in the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), and you have the opportunity to potentially receive loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). If you are passionate about Oregon's environment, apply today!

 *This is a full\-time, AFSCME represented position.*

*This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.*

**What are we looking for?**


6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field, with at least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities.

* *Bachelor’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 3 of the required years of experience.*
* *Master’s degree in physical science, environmental science, environmental engineering, natural resource engineering, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 4 of the required years of experience.*
* *Doctorate degree in physical science, environmental science, environmental engineering, natural resource engineering, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 5 of the required years of experience.*

jobs.description:
About Us 

We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 550+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. We are especially proud of our recent Great Place To Work® certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team member experiences. 
About The Role 

Rincon Consultants, Inc. is seeking a  Principal or Director, Stormwater & Watershed Sciences
 to lead and grow our construction and industrial stormwater quality services throughout California. 
This senior leadership role will focus on developing client programs related to California’s Construction and Industrial General Permits compliance, stormwater monitoring, SWPPP development and BMP implementation, regulatory strategy, and program management. The ideal candidate will be a strong seller-doer who can build client relationships, win work, provide senior technical leadership, and grow a high-performing practice. 
Candidates with broader experience in municipal stormwater and MS4 compliance, TMDLs, watershed management, and regional water quality programs will also have opportunities to support and expand Rincon’s broader Watershed Sciences practice. 
How We Collaborate

We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients. We may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office. Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  
What You’ll Do 

Lead and grow Rincon’s construction, industrial, and related stormwater quality services through strategic business development and client program expansion.

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Environmental Science, Geology, Water Resources, or a related field. 
​​​​​​​15+ years of progressively responsible experience in stormwater, water quality compliance, environmental consulting, or related services. 
Strong knowledge of California’s Construction General Permit and/or Industrial General Permit. 
Experience developing and managing large compliance programs with SWPPP implementation, BMP inspections, water quality sampling and monitoring, reporting, and corrective action planning. 
Proven business development experience, including cultivating client relationships, identifying opportunities, leading proposals, and winning work.

Strong business acumen and experience with budgets, staffing, scopes, contracts, and risk management.

Experience with municipal stormwater programs, MS4 permit compliance, TMDLs, watershed management, or regional water quality initiatives.

California PE, PG, or other relevant professional registration.

Experience developing multi-office or statewide client programs. 
Industry visibility through professional associations, conferences, publications, training, or related leadership activities.

Investing in You 

The base salary range for this full-time position is $150,000 to $200,000 plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Explore more about our culture, benefits, and life at Rincon on our Culture and Benefits page.

jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Exposure Assessment Specialist – Risk \& Air Modeling Group

**Job Overview** We are seeking a detail\-oriented Exposure Assessment Specialist to join our Risk \& Air Modeling Group. In this role, you will quantify and evaluate airborne particulate, chemical, and fiber exposures across consumer, occupational, and industrial environments. Primary focus areas include asbestos exposure (occupational and talc\-containing cosmetics), respirable crystalline silica (engineered stone/countertops), diesel particulate matter (railroad industry), and welding fumes. You will integrate analytical testing data, mathematical exposure models, and epidemiological literature to characterize risk profiles and support technical and legal evaluations.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Exposure \& Analytical Evaluation:** Review and interpret air sampling results, bulk analytical testing, and laboratory methodologies for asbestos, respirable crystalline silica, diesel particulate matter, and welding fumes.
* **Deposition \& Practice Review:** Analyze legal depositions, historical workplace conditions, and product use scenarios to reconstruct exposure duration, frequency, and intensity.
* **Epidemiological \& Scientific Synthesis:** Evaluate scientific literature, toxicological studies, and epidemiological data to benchmark exposure levels against health\-based thresholds and risk models.
* **Data Modeling \& Quantitative Analysis:** Apply mathematical formulas and spreadsheet\-based tools to calculate cumulative dose, airborne concentrations, and spatial exposure distributions.
* **Technical Reporting \& Communication:** Author comprehensive technical reports, exposure summaries, and visual presentations translating complex data for multidisciplinary teams and non\-technical stakeholders.

**Qualifications**

* **Education:** BA or BS in Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Health, Public Health, Environmental Engineering, or a related scientific field.
* **Quantitative \& Analytical Skills:** Strong applied mathematics background with demonstrated experience structuring exposure metrics and handling complex data sets.
* **Software Proficiency:** Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and Google Workspace (Sheets, Docs, Slides, Drive).
* **Technical Writing \& Synthesis:** Exceptional technical writing skills with a proven ability to distill dense analytical data into clear, defensible scientific documentation.
* **Communication:** Strong interpersonal and presentation skills to collaborate effectively within a fast\-paced risk and modeling team.

### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you looking to make a difference and join a highly motivated team working on issues critical to ensuring the safety and sustainability of California? The Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety’s Environmental Science Division is seeking an Environmental Scientist to analyze performance with vegetation management commitments in electrical utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMP).
  

The Environmental Science Division is responsible for evaluating the vegetation management aspects of utility WMPs, assessing performance in meeting vegetation management\-related commitments described in the WMPs, and ensuring that each utility is reducing its risk of igniting a catastrophic wildfire. To this end, Division scientists review regulatory filings and utility procedures, analyze reported data, perform audits, conduct field inspections, publish findings, and engage with the utilities and interested parties. Division scientists serve as subject\-matter experts in utility vegetation management and environmental policy related to wildfire risk reduction. Our team of scientists is highly collaborative and works closely with the Performance Assessment, Electric Safety Policy, and Data Analytics Divisions.  

  

  

Under general direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist Supervisor of the Inspections \& Investigations Branch the incumbent will inspect vegetation near electrical infrastructure, write inspection reports and plans to assess electrical corporation performance with approved Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMPs) and other regulatory requirements of the Department associated with forestry, wildfire science, and the environment. Incumbent will also investigate concerns raised by external parties and other potential WMP deficiencies, conduct critical and/or sensitive scientific investigations and studies and prepare guidance, planning, or regulatory documents on issues of importance to the department. Incumbent will organize and track inspection findings and identify issues found in the field, document the issues and elevate to the Supervisor with proposed recommendations. The incumbent will develop and maintain positive relationships with internal and external agency partners. The incumbent will be the subject matter expert on vegetation management programs to assess electrical utility performance with approved WMPs and other regulatory requirements of the Department associated with forestry, wildfire science, climate change and the environment.
  

  

The reporting location for this position is located at 3950 Paramount Boulevard, Suite 210, Lakewood, CA 90712\.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

jobs.description:
At the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, we deliver reliable water to a region with 19 million people—and to accomplish this, we rely on a team of talented employees: innovators, problem-solvers, and collaborators who make it all possible.

There is currently one (1) opening for Senior Environmental Specialist located at Union Station, Los Angeles, CA.

This recruitment may result in an eligibility list*.

Job Summary

The Senior Environmental Specialist leads the development, coordination, and implementation of complex environmental, health, and safety (EHS) compliance programs and technical studies across multiple Metropolitan sites. Serving as a technical subject matter expert, this role provides high-level program management and regulatory oversight across key disciplines including air quality, wastewater, stormwater, underground and aboveground storage tanks, hazardous materials and waste management, and health and safety. Based at the Los Angeles Headquarters, this position requires periodic travel and occasional overnight stays at field facilities throughout Southern California.

What You’ll Do

Program & Compliance Leadership: Formulate compliance strategies, secure environmental permits, and review changing legislation to assess organizational impacts. Monitor federal, state, and local regulations to minimize risk for employees, the environment, and the public.
Technical Systems & Data Tracking: Utilize specialized Environmental Management Information System (EMIS) software and online platforms—including, but not limited to: SCAQMD Permit Database, CARB DOORS/R3 databases, CERS, GeoTracker, LACPW EPIC system, CalOES Spill Reporting, and the DTSC Hazardous WasteTracking System—to manage compliance data and streamline cloud-based tracking tools.
Agency Collaboration & Liaison: Serve as a primary point of contact for regulatory agencies, local governments, and member agencies. Lead negotiations, respond to inquiries, and establish strong partnerships with internal and external entities to represent Metropolitan's operational interests.
Internal Partnership & Training: Partner with internal teams to evaluate day-to-day compliance, deliver technical expertise, make recommendations to supervisors, and design EHS awareness and training programs for personnel.
Reporting & Documentation: Conduct staff analyses, execute complex environmental studies, and prepare technical reports, general correspondence, and Board letters for management review.

Schedule:
9/80, Monday through Friday with every other Friday off

This job announcement has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work being performed by employees in this classification / job.

To view the full job description click here: Sr. Environmental Specialist

Schedule: 9/80
Start times are no earlier than 6 am and end times are no later than 6 pm.

Hybrid:
Metropolitan’s current practice in this position is a hybrid work schedule. This typically includes two days a week in person and the other days remote. This is subject to change dependent on organizational needs. In addition, a telework policy is scheduled for negotiations and once completed and implemented, will provide final direction on the hybrid schedule.

EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in environmental science, engineering, biology, ecology, planning, or other directly related field, and eight years of progressively responsible experience, including two years at the Environmental Specialist level or equivalent; or a master’s degree from an accredited college or university in environmental science, engineering, biology, ecology, planning, or other directly related field, and six years of progressively responsible experience including two years at the Environmental Specialist level or equivalent.

Relevant/Related Experience is defined as:
demonstrated experience serving as a lead for Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) programs, including managing multi-media environmental compliance areas such as Air Quality and Permitting, Underground Storage Tanks (UST), Industrial Wastewater, NPDES stormwater/wastewater reporting, and Hazardous Material Management.

Desirable Qualifications:

Environmental, Health, and Safety, Water Quality - Experience in public sector, water industry, public utilities; Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM); Certified Safety Professional (CSP); SCAQMD Certified Permitting Professional (CPP).

Certifications, Licenses, And Registration Requirements

License(s): Valid California Class C Driver’s License or equivalent (required at time of application) that allows you to drive during your employment.

CLOSING

Benefits

Competitive compensation
Excellent medical, dental, life, vision plans.
Deferred compensation in the form of a 401(k) plan (with matching contribution) and a 457 plan.
Retirement benefits under the California Public Employees' Retirement System
Tuition reimbursement
Training and advancement opportunities
Excellent working environment
Public transportation reimbursements
Hub of public transportation: rail, subway, buses, and taxis
On-site fitness center

jobs.title: Project Architect (Water Quality and R&D Labs)
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we’re helping to shape the future of cities by delivering innovative, sustainable solutions that elevate the way people live, work, and connect. Our California Cities & Places team partners with clients across the public and private sectors to create spaces that are functional, resilient, and inspiring. As we continue to expand our architectural practice in California, we’re seeking a Project Architect
based out of Los Angeles, Irvine, or San Francisco, CA
, to help lead transformative design projects that positively impact communities.

Our Project Architect’s support and lead our design teams while working with clients in preparing designs, completing construction documents, develop building plans, code reviews, writes specifications and develops the presentation of materials. This role is centered around Life Science R&D facilities, Water/Wastewater (Water Quality Labs), but will also work across other markets and project types.

Please note
This is a hybrid position and will require you to be in the office 2-3 days a week typically with travel to construction site locations in Northern or Southern California (depending on applicants location) on a regular basis.

What You’ll Do

Serve as a Project Architect on medium-to-large, complex architectural projects across the Cities & Places market.
Lead the architectural design and technical development from early concept through construction documentation and construction contract administration with guidance and oversight/mentorship from Senior Architects.
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams including architecture, engineering, planning, interiors, and specialty consultants.
Facilitate client presentations, design reviews, and stakeholder engagement activities.
Interpret and apply local, state, and national building codes (e.g., IBC, IFC, ADA, NFPA, local amendments)
Provide code analysis and compliance strategies during project planning, design development, and construction
Lead architectural design team efforts for construction phase services, providing or overseeing Jacobs’ responses to RFIs, submittal and shop drawing reviews, construction modification documents, and site visit/observations.
Lead the architectural team members on the project in planning deliverables alongside the project design schedules, and quality standards to ensure alignment with scope and client expectations.
Mentor and guide junior architects and designers, fostering a collaborative project environment.
Partner with project managers to manage design risk, resolve technical challenges, and ensure successful execution.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Architecture
Licensed Architect (California)
Minimum 15 years of architectural experience, including experience leading complex, multi-disciplinary building and infrastructure design projects.
Working knowledge of model/rendering and design tools (including REVIT, AutoCAD, Enscape, Adobe Creative Suite, BIM360, Navisworks, Bluebeam Revu).
Experience working with California-specific utility agencies and municipalities. Experience working with private-sector Science & Tech clients on R&D Lab projects
Deep understanding of building codes and their application to projects in the Science & Tech, Industrial, and Water/Wastewater markets
Understanding of integration of building services, building core, and envelope elements and where these relate to the previously mentioned markets.
Experience leading ground-up new build and Core & Shell as well as ‘warm-shell’ interior fit-out projects working alongside a core & shell/developer team.
Comfort working in a fast paced, collaborative project environment including ground-up and Tenant Improvement projects.
Experience coordinating multidisciplinary design teams
Strong organizational, communications (verbal, written as well as hand sketching) skills, and leadership abilities are required

Ideally, You’ll Also Have

Experience with alternative delivery models Design-Build, Progressive-Design-Build, CMAR, P3, Integrated Project Delivery, etc
Strong design sensibility combined with technical expertise.
Experience with sustainable design frameworks (LEED, WELL, Envision, etc.).
Demonstrated ability to lead project teams and mentor emerging professionals.

Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $143,000.00 to $184,900.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on May 12, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better.
