jobs.description:
Position/Program Information

Exam Number

PH5672G-EA

Type Of Recruitment

OPEN COMPETITIVE - EMERGENCY

First Day Of Filing

The application filing period will begin on Tu
esday, September 1, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. , (PT) - Continuous.

We will keep accepting applications until the position is filled. The application window may close unexpectedly once we have enough qualified candidates.

The LA County Board of Supervisors recently declared a local state of emergency for homelessness , and the County is working to revise and expand our response to help all who are affected. We are looking for qualified and passionate individuals to help us in the mission of addressing issues like housing, mental health, and substance use. If you are looking for a new career that will directly benefit the population of LA County, this may be the opportunity for you.

The County of Los Angeles Department of Public Health is seeking qualified candidates to fill emergency Environmental Health Specialist III vacancies related to the homelessness crisis.

Under the emergency order, applicants who meet the requirements may be hired for an initial period of up to 90 days, with an opportunity for permanent County employment.

During your initial work period, you will be assessed on your work performance. This assessment will be weighted 100%.

Those who successfully pass the assessment will be considered for permanent appointment to Environmental Health Specialist III.

Definition

Performs specialized environmental health inspections and investigations of complex environmental health problems; or provides lead supervision to field staff who are enforcing environmental health and consumer protection laws by making inspections, initiating investigations and taking appropriate enforcement action.

For information about the specific classification standards for this position, please visit the following link : Environmental Health Specialist III

Essential Job Functions

What will I do as an Environmental Health Specialist III?

Conducts periodic specialized technical field inspections and investigations of manufacturing, industrial, or other large scale facilities and institutions in such areas as food and drug, water, sewage control, multiple housing and institutions, garment manufacturing, laundering facilities, public swimming facilities, water pollution control and dairies and milk products plants to determine compliance with relevant public health laws and regulations; completes reports of areas in violation.
Verifies the proper manufacture, storage, preparation and transportation of foods, drugs, and dairy products ensuring process is free from contamination, adulteration, or mislabeling; investigating suspected food poisonings and other complaints; inspecting such facilities as hotels, motels, jails, mental institutions, multiple housing, and boarding homes for compliance with established environmental standards; approving plans for the construction of public swimming facilities and the installation and maintenance of facility equipment; ensuring that potable water meets Federal, State, local, physical, chemical, and bacteriological standards; approving sewage disposal installations and inspecting water treatment, sewage disposal and water reclamation plants; and conducting specialized testing procedures to ensure that no potentially dangerous connections exist between industrial equipment, industrial processing water and plumbing fixtures whereby toxic chemicals, sewage or contaminated water could be introduced into the domestic water supply system.
Meets with concerned parties from private industry and companies to provide current information on environmental procedures and public health laws, to discuss correction of deficiencies, to develop a corrective plan, and to obtain compliance through appropriate enforcement action, including quarantine, embargo, condemnation of food or drug products, the issuance of citations, and the confiscation of evidence of violation including equipment, and by providing expert testimony in criminal prosecution.
Develops and implements staff development and training programs designed to provide Environmental Health staff with current information on environmental health procedures and public health laws, and to improve the quality of environmental health inspections, investigations, and services to the public.
Performs administrative studies or analyses of public health laws and ordinances by comparing Federal, State, and local codes in a specific area such as food service to determine their impact on environmental health programs and operating methods.
Provides technical direction to district environmental staff who are inspecting, investigating, and enforcing laws pertaining to environmental health and consumer protection by reviewing work, both administratively and in the field, advising on methods and techniques applied, and determining their effectiveness in enforcing applicable public health laws.
Conducts special investigations such as food poisoning; or provides support in the resolution of the more difficult investigations.
Reviews the preparation of evidence for the prosecution of environmental health cases on non-compliance with public health laws and regulations by ensuring that subordinate staff have prepared samples of adulterated foods according to prescribed methods, that the findings of tests conducted by laboratory technicians are available and in the prescribed format and that all material required by city or the District Attorney for prosecution has been provided.
Act in the absence of the District Chief Environmental Health Specialist, as needed.

Requirements

REQUIREMENTS TO QUALIFY:

Two (2) years' experience as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist for a health department.

License(s) & Certificate(s) Required

Certificate as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist issued by the California State Department of Public Health.*
A valid California Class C Driver License is required to carry out job-related essential functions.**

Physical Class

Physical Class III - Moderate: I ncludes standing or walking most of the time, with bending, stooping, squatting, twisting, and reaching; includes working on irregular surfaces, occasionally lifting objects weighing over 25 pounds, and frequent lifting of 10-25 pounds.

Special Requirement Information

You MUST
meet the above requirement(s) in order to be appointed to fill any vacancies related to this recruitment.

You MUST submit a legible copy of the original certificate (not the pocket license) as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist issued by the California Department of Public Health with your application at the time of filing or email a copy within seven (7) calendar days of filing to HRExams@ph.lacounty.gov or your application will be rejected as incomplete.
For information on how to obtain the certificate as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist from the California State Department of Public Health, call (916) 449-5661 or click on the following link : https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CEH/DRSEM/Pages/EMB/REHS/REHS.asp
You MUST submit a copy of your valid California Class C Driver License with your application at the time of filing or email a copy within seven (7) calendar days of filing to HRExams@ph.lacounty.gov or your application will be rejected as incomplete.
Successful applicants for positions that require driving must obtain and present a copy of his/her driving record from the California Department of Motor Vehicles before final appointment. Applicants should not present a copy of their driving history until asked to do so by the hiring department. The County will make an individualized assessment of whether an applicant’s driving history has a direct or adverse relationship with the specific duties of the job. License must not be currently suspended, restricted, or revoked.

Additional Information

EXAMINATION CONTENT:

During your initial work period, the appointing department will evaluate your performance. Those who achieve a passing score on this evaluation will be considered for permanent appointment.

_______________________________________________________________

Application and Filing Information

How To Apply

Applications must be filed
ONLINE ONLY

and will be reviewed for interview consideration on an ongoing basis. Position/Program Information

Exam Number

PH5671G-EA

Type Of Recruitment

First Day Of Filing

The application filing period will begin on Tuesday, September 1, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. (PT) - Continuous.

We will keep accepting applications until the position is filled. The application window may close unexpectedly once we have enough qualified candidates.

The LA County Board of Supervisors recently declared a local state of emergency for homelessness , and the County is working to revise and expand our response to help all who are affected. We are looking for qualified and passionate individuals to help us in the mission of addressing issues like housing, mental health, and substance use. If you are looking for a new career that will directly benefit the population of LA County, this may be the opportunity for you.

The County of Los Angeles Department of Public Health is seeking qualified candidates to fill emergency Environmental Health Specialist II vacancies related to the homelessness crisis.

Under the emergency order, applicants who meet the requirements may be hired for an initial period of up to 90 days, with an opportunity for permanent County employment.

During your initial work period, you will be assessed on your work performance. This assessment will be weighted 100%.

Those who successfully pass the assessment will be considered for permanent appointment to Environmental Health Specialist II.

Definition

Enforces environmental health and consumer protection laws by making inspections, conducting investigations, and taking appropriate enforcement action.

For information about the specific classification standards for this position, please visit the following link: Environmental Health Specialist II
.

Essential Job Functions

What will I do as an Environmental Health Specialist II?

Conducts periodic inspections of food establishments and restaurants to ensure legal compliance and to promote environment health by making observations to see that food is unadulterated, properly labeled, refrigerated, stored, handled, and protected from contaminants.
Reviews and observes utensil washing and sanitizing procedures by testing water temperatures and cleaning agents and facilities to ensure that these meet Federal, State, and local legal requirements.
Ensures that food equipment such as stoves, refrigerators, and other cooking equipment and appliances are clean and in good repair and takes appropriate enforcement action; completes reports of areas in violation.
Investigates complaints concerning the infestation of rodents and insects by looking for evidence of infestation such as telltale signs and avenues of entry, placing poisons, recommending corrective measures, and taking appropriate enforcement action.
Conducts periodic inspections and investigates complaints concerning the improper disposal of garbage, rubbish, and sewage and other unsanitary conditions in building, multiple and single family dwellings, and retail food or other establishments by conducting inspections of premises for adequate disposal facilities, such as covered bins to prevent insect and rodent infestation; recommends corrective measures and takes appropriate enforcement action.
Conducts specialized technical inspections and investigations to prevent and control consumer fraud in the retail marketing and sale of food under public health laws and regulations concerned with adulteration, mislabeling, and false advertising of food; meets with concerned parties to discuss correction of deficiencies and to obtain compliance through appropriate enforcement action.
Initiates and participates in prosecution of environmental health cases of non-compliance with public health laws and regulations by completing investigation reports, securing evidence, taking and collecting photographs, and preparing cases for prosecution, initiating and attending office hearings, and conferring with city or the District Attorney.
Participates in communicable disease investigations related to environmental health.
Ensures that establishments being inspected have obtained a current public health license or permit: ensures that establishments receive and post a grade/score card.
Maintains rapport with community organizations and may serve as a member of the organization's formal structure to provide guidance on environmental health related problems.
Testifies in court as the investigating officer for the Department of Health Services, as needed.
Drives a personal vehicle to and from various locations throughout the County to carry out job related essential functions.

If you have permanent status and have passed probation, you have mandatory reinstatement rights into your former position/classification at the end of this LT appointment.You will be separated from state service if you have not had prior permanent or probationary civil service status. During this 12\-month limited\-term assignment, you may be entitled to receive health, dental, and vision benefits. You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.  

  

  



The Regulatory Development Section (RDS) within the Monitoring and Laboratory Division (MLD) is seeking a highly skilled Staff Air Pollution Specialist to help implement a multi\-agency pilot program involving the repurposing of crude oil and natural gas wells and production infrastructure for energy storage and generation.  

Senate Bill (SB) 567, authored by Senator Monique Limón and signed into law in October of 2025, establishes the Gravity Based Energy Storage Well Pilot Program, which will sunset on January 1, 2035\. It authorizes the conversion of 250 idle crude oil and natural gas wells to gravity\-based energy storage systems. Under SB 567, CARB will collaborate with the Department of Conservation, California Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) and the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) to establish criteria for mechanical integrity testing, continuous leak monitoring of air pollutants, and reporting protocols. CARB will also serve as a key technical and policy advisor alongside CalGEM, SWRCB, and interested parties to evaluate the pilot’s progress and to include recommendations whether to continue the Gravity\-Based Energy Storage Well Program.

This position is a special and unique opportunity to work in some of the most beautiful watersheds in the state of California, studying and enhancing salmon and steelhead populations primarily in the Eel River and watersheds of the Mendocino Coast. Work is related to state and federal Endangered Species Act listed stocks and management of valued fisheries for the state and tribes on the North Coast. Promoting collaboration with partners in order to leverage collective resources is encouraged. This position stands to make a positive and real difference for trust resources and those that value them. Under the general guidance of the Coastal Fisheries Environmental Program Manager, the incumbent supervises the Coastal Watershed Planning and Assessment Program. The Program includes a broad suite of monitoring, assessment, restoration, and regulatory activities in Humboldt and Mendocino Counties. These activities include monitoring and assessment of fish life history, fish distribution, recovery, permitting, ecosystem assessment, restoration planning, and annual sportfish regulations. This position will oversee or support various aquatic resource plans, restoration and monitoring plans, and several monitoring and assessment activities related specifically to the Eel River and potential dam removal. The incumbent manages a complex budget, helps develop and manage large scale ecosystem assessments, and develops and manages complex contracts or grants with ecological scope. As such the position entails significant grant/contract writing and management responsibilities. This includes planning, directing, and coordinating all aspects of development and implementation of detailed and watershed\-specific monitoring and research programs for salmon, steelhead, and other trout populations. Responsibilities are varied and include analyzing complex environmental issues, requiring a high level of personal initiative in the application of sound scientific methods and ecological principles to natural resource assessment, management, planning and habitat restoration activities. Incumbent will represent the Department in dealings with local, State and federal governmental agencies, Tribal partners, conservation groups and private landowners. Area of geographic responsibility includes all nine Northern California counties that make up the Northern Region, however duties will be largely focused in Humboldt and Mendocino Counties. Performance of specified duties requires a comprehensive knowledge of administrative procedures, Department policies, applicable environmental law, and complex ecological principals. Contacts made in the course of this work are highly sensitive and involve a wide degree of interests. jobs.description:
Job Overview:

At the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, we deliver reliable water to a region with 19 million people—and to accomplish this, we rely on a team of talented employees: innovators, problem\-solvers, and collaborators who make it all possible.  

This recruitment may result in an **Eligibility List\***.  

The Environmental Specialist serves as an advanced, journey\-level technical expert responsible for planning, conducting, coordinating, and monitoring complex environmental studies and projects for the Metropolitan Water District.  

At this recognized specialist level, you will be responsible for ensuring compliance with source and treated water regulations with a strong focus on invasive mussel control and emerging regulations. You will spearhead the agency's strategic response to invasive mussels in source waters and ensure compliance with relevant environmental and water quality regulations, California Department of Fish and Wildlife mandates, and invasive species frameworks.  

You will also be responsible for tracking and ensuring compliance with environmental permitting and pesticide regulations, considerations for raw water releases, contributing to agency responses to federal and state regulatory developments, hazardous waste management, various aspects of source water protection, and preparing reports, response plans, and research proposals.  

Daily duties include monitoring pertinent environmental laws, codes, regulations, and pending litigation that impact operations, as well as drafting actionable, high\-level strategies and responses to address operational requirements and regulatory developments.  

Candidates must possess a bachelor's degree in environmental science, biology, chemistry, or a related field, supplemented by six years of progressive, professional environmental compliance experience that demonstrates mastery over multi\-agency coordination and permitting and complex project management. **What You’ll Do:*** Lead agency response to invasive mussels in source water infrastructure.
* Develop control strategies to prevent and mitigate infrastructure and biological impacts.
* Coordinate monitoring programs for invasive species.
* Ensure compliance with state and federal water quality, environmental, and invasive species regulations.
* Coordinate complex studies regarding environmental planning and regulatory compliance.
* Track pertinent laws, regulations, codes, and pending litigation.
* Analyze operational impacts of emerging environmental policies and regulations on Metropolitan.
* Represent the agency in meetings with stakeholders and serve as point\-of\-contact with regulators and outside agencies.
* Communicate and coordinate with member agencies on relevant environmental and water quality issues.

**The Opportunity:**


Tetra Tech, Inc is currently seeking a motivated, detail\-oriented Entry\-Level Environmental Specialist to support environmental consulting projects across a range of sectors, including regulatory compliance, field investigations, environmental permitting, and reporting. This position is ideal for a recent graduate or early\-career professional who is eager to build a career in environmental consulting and contribute to meaningful projects that support responsible development and environmental stewardship.

**Why Tetra Tech:**


At Tetra Tech, we are *Leading with Science* to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry\-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting\-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

**Your Impact:**


Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting\-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world\-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

**Essential Job Functions:**


The Environmental Specialist will work under the guidance of experienced staff and project managers to assist with field work, data collection, technical documentation, and client deliverables. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong communication skills, a willingness to learn, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.

* Support preparation of technical reports, permit applications, compliance documents, and environmental deliverables.

* Conduct literature and regulatory research related to environmental permitting and compliance.

* Follow health, safety, and quality assurance protocols during field and office work.
* Support senior staff with project coordination, scheduling, and client communication as needed.
* Travel to project sites as required for field assignments.
* Perform other duties as assigned.


**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Geology, Natural Resources, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
* 0–2 years of relevant experience, including internships, co\-ops, or field research.

* Ability to organize information, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines.
* Willingness to work outdoors in varying weather and field conditions.

* Fieldwork may occur outdoors in a variety of weather conditions, including heat, cold, wind, rain, snow, and dust. Field locations may include construction sites, industrial facilities, undeveloped land, wetlands, streams, roadways, or remote project areas.

The California Department of Fish and Wildlife's Northern Region office in Redding is hiring an Environmental Scientist to lead our field efforts of the Heritage and Wild Trout Program.

Field sites include world class fisheries such a Eagle Lake, the McCloud River, Sacramento River, Hat Creek, Fall River, and more, with opportunities to explore and development Northern California's many other wild trout fishing opportunities. ### **Job Description and Duties**


The California Coastal Commission is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist or Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to join its Ecology Team (Technical Services Unit) at its Headquarters Office in downtown San Francisco. This position will primarily focus on the relationship between wildfire and coastal ecology as relates to vegetation management for fuel reduction, ecological restoration, and resilience work across a range of ecosystems, including forests, shrublands, grasslands and wetlands throughout the coastal zone, which extends inland from the shoreline at variable distances up to more than five miles in some areas.


The Commission is a small State agency that is charged with protecting coastal resources and managing coastal development in California. The Commission’s mission is to implement the Coastal Act and to protect, restore, and enhance coastal and marine resources for the continuing benefit of current and future generations. It carries out this mandate through regulatory and planning actions related to development within offshore waters and on land along the California coast. The Commission also has authority under the federal Coastal Zone Management Act to review federal and federally\-permitted activities such as dredging, military training exercises, wildland management, and highway projects that affect resources of the coastal zone.


The Ecology Team generally supports the Commission and its staff with technical review and analysis of potential effects on the coast’s sensitive natural resources associated with proposed development projects. Under the direction of the Ecology Team Manager, the successful incumbent will be integrated into the existing team of five ecologists and work with Commission staff to address ecological issues raised in the Commission’s policy, planning, and regulatory work as relates to wildfire resilience and risk reduction efforts. This work will focus on understanding and addressing the ecological effects of vegetation management for fuel reduction and wildfire resilience, including through ecological restoration, throughout the coastal zone. It will necessitate cooperation with other scientific and technical teams such as Mapping and Water Quality, coordination with the Commission’s Statewide Planning Unit, and provision of scientific support to staff and the Commission. Duties will be adjusted commensurately to the level at which the position is filled. Generally, the incumbent will be expected to: review and analyze a variety of technical reports including CEQA/NEPA documents, technical surveys and memoranda, restoration and mitigation plans, and scientific literature; conduct research and investigations often involving complex environmental conditions and circumstances; identify problems including potential adverse impacts to coastal resources and means to avoid and minimize these; factor in climate change dynamics relative to environmental considerations; coordinate with other federal, state, and local agencies; and, make recommendations for conformance with the natural resource policies of the Coastal Act and relevant certified plans.


Key functions of the job include: analyzing proposed fire resilience and risk reduction work for consistency with applicable Coastal Act policies; tracking topical scientific literature including white papers and peer\-reviewed publications; guiding related policy based on scientific understanding of the issues and existing frameworks; developing recommendations on how to avoid and minimize adverse impacts to native habitat (including for communities and species) associated with fuel reduction and vegetation management efforts across the landscape while advancing ecological resilience; contributing to the development of recommendations for Commission regulatory action, including staff reports, permit conditions, and planning documents; communicating with project proponents; updating and maintaining a spatial database of authorized fire resilience and risk reduction work and conducting geospatial analyses; reviewing monitoring and mitigation plans and reports; participating in site visits and inspections to evaluate on\-the\-ground ecological conditions; writing technical memoranda to support and accompany staff reports and recommendations; and providing technical presentations at public meetings. The incumbent may also represent the Commission staff on multi\-agency work groups, task forces, and similar entities; and coordinate with staff of local, state, and federal agencies; the legislature; stakeholder groups; and the broader public.


The position offers considerable opportunity for developing and contributing expertise on a range of ecosystems as well as relevant and emerging issues related to coastal ecology and wildfire resilience in California’s coastal landscape.

### **Job Description and Duties**


**Per CCR 249\.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**  

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist will conduct environmental health inspections of facilities housing egg\-laying hens, calves raised for veal, and breeding pigs to ensure conformance with confinement standards, gather scientific data on food\-animal housing and confinement systems, research and investigate complaints or incidents of farm animal cruelty due to improper housing and care, as well as misbranded products from noncompliant sources, provide analytical expertise and reports on specific livestock confinement parameters on egg\-laying farms, pig breeding facilities, and veal calf production operations, and conduct inspections and audits of distributors, retailers and other end\-users for traceable records of shipments from compliant sources. The Environmental Scientist (ES) will enforce complex environmental health and safety laws and regulations, and execute policies and procedures to improve environmental health, the humane confinement and care of food\-producing animals, and the sustainability of California agriculture.
  

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!  

  

  

Be a part of the Animal Care Program team and travel throughout California to ensure Animal Confinement laws and regulations are implemented and enforced.  

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The duties of this position require the employee to work in the field approximately 70% of the time. This 70% of time includes traveling to locations both inside and outside of California, which includes air travel and overnight travel when necessary. The employee reports to the Sacramento Office, Headquarters Location (at minimum on a quarterly basis), only to pick up supplies, attend meetings and turn in required documents. Travel expenses from the employee’s home to their assigned Headquarters Location are considered a normal commute and are not reimbursable.  

Regular field work involves travel via car throughout California and to various locations across the lower 48 states. Travel for work may include air travel up to three times per month.  

When working in the field the employee may be exposed to extremes in temperatures and high noise levels in a variety of environments ranging from individual farm premises to complex, multi\-story product handling, packaging, and distribution centers. Indoor locations may include food handling and processing facilities, as well as food retail settings.  

The employee is required to comply with all Departmental Health and Safety Protocols, including the use of appropriate personal protective equipment, participation in required medical clearance, and adherence to safety procedures during field and office duties.  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While the CDFA supports telework where possible, in\-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.

**The Opportunity:**
Tetra Tech is adding a highly motivated ***Environmental Compliance Project Manager*** to join our growing energy compliance and site restoration practice. This team supports environmental compliance monitoring, restoration ecology, revegetation, and restoration science activities associated with utility\-scale renewable energy generation, transmission, and infrastructure projects.  

The successful candidate will manage environmental compliance and restoration projects from planning and permitting through construction and early operations. This position offers opportunities to work with multidisciplinary teams, regulatory agencies, contractors, and clients on some of the most significant renewable energy projects throughout the western United States. **Location:** Flexible within the Western United States (Remote or Hybrid) **Why Tetra Tech:**
At Tetra Tech, we are *Leading with Science* to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry\-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting\-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world. **Your Impact:**
Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting\-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world\-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy. **Your Role:****Project Management*** Manage environmental compliance and restoration projects from initiation through completion.
* Develop and manage project scopes, schedules, budgets, forecasts, and deliverables.
* Coordinate project teams consisting of environmental scientists, biologists, restoration specialists, and subcontractors.
* Monitor project performance and ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with client expectations.
* Support proposal preparation, work planning, staffing coordination, and project forecasting.

**Environmental Compliance \& Restoration*** Manage environmental compliance activities during pre\-construction, construction, and early operational phases of utility\-scale energy projects.
* Oversee environmental monitors, restoration crews, and revegetation contractors.
* Monitor site conditions and ensure compliance with permit requirements and environmental commitments.
* Support restoration planning, implementation, monitoring, and adaptive management efforts.
* Evaluate restoration performance and provide recommendations for corrective actions when necessary.

**Agency \& Stakeholder Coordination*** Coordinate with federal, state, and local agencies regarding project compliance requirements.
* Support public outreach and stakeholder engagement efforts.
* Interpret permit requirements and land use regulations and communicate compliance obligations to project teams.
* Interface regularly with clients, contractors, regulatory agencies, and project stakeholders.

**Technical Leadership*** Provide technical guidance related to restoration ecology, revegetation, environmental compliance, and construction monitoring.
* Review technical reports, compliance documentation, monitoring reports, and restoration plans.
* Support development of environmental compliance strategies and best management practices.
* Ensure technical deliverables meet company quality standards.

**Professional Development \& Safety*** Conduct activities in accordance with company procedures, legislation, permit conditions, and industry standards.
* Promote and support a strong health and safety culture.
* Maintain professional expertise through continuing education and industry involvement.
* Report health and safety concerns and incidents promptly.

jobs.title: Air Quality Managing Consultant
jobs.location: North Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
Job Description

Position Description

We are seeking an experienced air quality professional to provide technical leadership and project delivery support within Ramboll’s Air and Climate Service Line. This position will focus on complex air dispersion modelling, air quality impact assessment, client advisory services, project management, and mentoring of junior to mid-level colleagues.

The role offers an opportunity to contribute to a growing national air quality practice while working collaboratively across Australian and global teams. Candidates with experience in digital tools, data workflows, automation, GIS, or cross-region technical coordination will be well placed to support ongoing innovation in how air quality services are delivered.

Air Quality Managing Consultant

Working within the Air and Climate Service Line you will be responsible for identifying, conducting and developing air quality projects based on an understanding of business needs, challenges, opportunities and the marketplace. Ramboll is seeking an experienced Air Quality Modelling professional for this position. Our ideal candidate is a technical leader with a proven track record of managing complex, multi-faceted air quality modelling projects, mentoring junior staff, and serving as a trusted advisor to clients. You would be responsible for overseeing project staff and be responsible for project delivery across the air quality team.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Technical Leadership: Lead and deliver complex air quality dispersion modelling and environmental impact assessment projects using regulatory and specialist models such as AERMOD, CALPUFF, CALMET, GRAL/GRAMM, TAPM and WRF. Develop innovative approaches to solving complex air quality, odour, emissions inventory and post-processing challenges.
Project Management: Manage air quality projects, including scope, schedule, budget, resources and quality, to support on-time and on-budget delivery that meets client expectations. Supervise project teams and delegate tasks to junior staff as required.
Technical Review and Quality Assurance: Provide senior-level QA/QC review and technical oversight of modelling analyses, emissions inventories, impact assessments, management plans, approval inputs and technical reports prepared by project teams.
Client and Regulatory Engagement: Act as a trusted client advisor through the full project lifecycle, from early strategy and scoping through approvals, compliance and implementation. Lead or support technical discussions with regulators and approval authorities on behalf of clients.
Staff Mentoring and Development: Mentor junior to mid-level air quality staff by providing technical guidance, training, review and career development support.
Business Development: Contribute technical and business content to proposals, develop scopes of work, support strategic client engagement and identify opportunities for growth in air quality services.
Digital and Cross-Region Collaboration: Support efficient project delivery through digital and technical innovation coordinating with Australian, APAC and global colleagues where specialist input or shared capability is required.

You will be part of the Australian Air and Climate Service Line working within the Air Quality Team as a Managing Consultant. You will lead the delivery of air quality projects, providing technical leadership, project management, and mentoring to junior team members, while supporting the ongoing growth and development of Ramboll’s national air quality capability.

Reporting to the National Air and Climate Practice Lead, you will play a key role in strengthening Ramboll’s air quality services and contributing to the continued success of the team. The position offers the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across Australia, APAC and our global network to enhance project delivery, provide specialist technical expertise, drive digital innovation and promote technical excellence across Ramboll’s national air quality team.

Qualifications

About You

From the moment you start we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills and capabilities that will set you up for success:

Bachelor or Post Graduate degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering or related field with minimum 10 years of experience in air dispersion modelling and impact assessment.
Certified Air Quality Professional (CAQP) with the Clean Air Society of Australia and New Zealand and demonstrated involvement in profile raising activities (preferred).
Proficiency in meteorological and air dispersion modelling software such as AERMET, AERMOD, CALMET, CALPUFF, GRAMM, GRAL, TAPM and WRF.
Experience in development of air, odour and GHG emissions inventories across a wide range of industry sectors.
Strong technical knowledge and report writing skills, including preparation of Air Quality Impact Assessments, monitoring reports, Air Quality Management Plans and proposals.
Experienced project management skills, including direct client engagement. Business development skills are highly desirable, as is demonstrated experience in people management and/or mentoring.
Experience in ambient air quality monitoring, stack testing knowledge, climate risk assessment and/or noise monitoring and modelling, is not essential but would be highly regarded.
Experience in the following fields is highly desirable, including GIS software (e.g. ArcGIS Pro and Surfer), programming (e.g. R and Python), and analytical and data visualisation platforms (e.g. MS Power BI).
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical, digital or data-related information clearly to clients, regulators and multidisciplinary project teams.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Interesting and diverse projects
The opportunity to work with some of the best and brightest professionals in your field
Flexible work arrangements
Investment in your development
Leaders you can count on, guided by our Leadership Principles
Appreciation for the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects.

We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So, if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll employs more than 18,000 people globally across 35 countries. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, Management Consulting, and Architecture & Landscape. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we help shape the societies of tomorrow.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics. Please let us know if there are any changes, we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

jobs.description:
**Position overview Position title:** Assistant Professor Salary range: The current salary range for this position is $84,100–$132,900 (9\-month academic year salary), however, off\-scale salary and other components of pay, which would yield compensation that is higher than this range, are offered to meet competitive conditions. Anticipated start: July 1, 2027 Application Window
  
**Open date:** August 24, 2026
  
**Next review date:** Friday, Oct 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.
  
**Final date:** Friday, Oct 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date. Position description
  
The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management (ESPM) at the University of California, Berkeley (UCB) invites applications for a tenure\-track Assistant Professor nine\-month faculty position in the area of Arthropod Biodiversity.
  
Biodiversity lies at the heart of all ecosystems, from the smallest microbiomes to the global expanses of continents, oceans, and the atmosphere. It holds intrinsic value across many dimensions, encompassing species, genes, functions, processes, and cultures, while also providing tangible benefits such as food, medicine, and other natural products. Biodiversity underpins essential ecosystem services, including clean air, water, and soil, and contributes profoundly to human health, cultural identity, and psychological well\-being. Arthropods, which E.O. Wilson famously described as “the little things that run the world,” are the majority of Earth's macrobiota and have recently faced threats from multiple stressors, including climate change, habitat loss and degradation, and cumulative use of agricultural chemicals.
  
Loss of biodiversity, both locally (α\-diversity) and among locations (β\-diversity) is occurring at a rate exceeding our current efforts to discover, document, and understand the species with which we share our planet. These patterns are particularly true for arthropods, with insects showing global declines in populations across multiple orders (sometimes referred to as “insect apocalypse”). At the species level, arthropods now represent 70\-80% of the documented loss of biodiversity. At the same time, many other arthropods are becoming increasingly problematic as invasive species, pests of agriculture and forests, and vectors of plant and animal pathogens. Expertise is needed in understanding drivers of arthropod biodiversity change, including understanding processes leading to resilient populations, communities, and ecosystems.
  
ESPM is a multidisciplinary community of scholars from across the sciences and humanities who conduct research, teaching, and outreach to advance scientific understanding and develop solutions for the world's pressing environmental problems. ESPM is home to a top\-ranked Ph.D. program in environmental science, environmental studies, and ecological/evolutionary biology. Our undergraduate students have a choice of vibrant majors that span the disciplines in the department.
  
ESPM is committed to addressing the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples and single parents. We are also interested in candidates who have had non\-traditional career paths, who have taken time off for family reasons, or who have achieved excellence in careers outside academia. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website .
  
**Department :** https://ourenvironment.berkeley.edu/ Qualifications Basic qualifications (required at time of application)
  
Applicants for this position must hold a Ph.D. (or equivalent international degree) or be enrolled in a Ph.D. (or equivalent international degree) granting program at the time of application. Preferred qualifications
  
The successful applicant will develop an internationally recognized research and teaching program focusing on terrestrial arthropod biodiversity in studies of (but not limited to) ecology, arthropod data science, disease biology, community/ecosystem ecology, conservation biology, systematics, evolutionary biology, and biological interventions (including management, removals, biological control, bioremediation, restoration, climate\-adaptation). We encourage applicants whose research contributes to the design, management, and integrated understanding of biodiverse systems, using any of many approaches, including (but not limited to) field surveys, use and integration of natural history collections, ecological manipulations, genomics, AI, and computational biology.
  
The successful candidate will have a doctoral degree in a relevant field such as, but not limited to, biological disciplines (including ecology, evolutionary biology, conservation biology, systematics), environmental sciences, geography, entomology, or related fields. The successful candidate will demonstrate:
  
Expertise in any area of terrestrial (non\-marine) arthropod biodiversity research.
  
Organismal expertise (e.g., ecological, evolutionary, systematic, etc.) in a taxon or group of taxa in any habitat, including but not limited to terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems, including working landscapes.
  
The ability to establish an innovative research agenda in partnership with other disciplines.
  
An interest in participatory research with practitioners and communities and the translation of science into solutions via policy and/or partnerships with government agencies, NGOs, or business.
  
Strong research productivity, potential for external funding, and a commitment to excellence in teaching.
  
Commitment to supporting the success of all students with effective mentoring and innovative classroom pedagogy.
  
Willingness to engage in service and leadership activities within the University and their profession. Application Requirements Document requirement

Join a growing Queensland environmental team where you will influence major infrastructure, energy, water, defence and resource projects while shaping environmental outcomes for regional communities. We have several long\-term environmental programs in Central QLD and numerous opportunities for work across multiple sectors that will benefit from your environmental expertise.


CQG Consulting (CQG) has recently become part of Beca, one of Asia Pacific’s largest independent advisory, design and engineering consultancies. Together CQG and Beca are strengthening our environmental science, ecology, GIS, stakeholder engagement, planning and approvals capability across regional Queensland. Both CQG and Beca have built their businesses on trusted relationships, outcome\-focused advice and a strong understanding of their clients and the communities in which they work.


**The Opportunity**

We are looking for an experienced **Environmental Scientist** to lead our environmental monitoring programs. The role will see you design and manage monitoring programs, coordinate teams, interpret environmental data, assess compliance and prepare high\-quality scientific reports. Providing technical leadership across monitoring programs, with the opportunity to work on major infrastructure, energy, water, Defence and resource projects.


You will be responsible for the effective delivery of environmental monitoring programs, particularly surface water and groundwater monitoring, and assess the data for Environmental Authority compliance reporting.


While this is primarily a program management, technical and reporting role, you will need a strong practical understanding of environmental field sampling and equipment. You will occasionally undertake or oversee field activities, particularly where technical expertise, troubleshooting or quality assurance is required.


You will also play an important role in ensuring junior staff and field teams are applying appropriate sampling techniques and quality assurance procedures.

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/ .

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here .

Role Description

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC) , advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. This position is responsible for overseeing the development of high quality educational and interpretive programs, and ensuring a welcoming and meaningful experience for all visitors. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position works collaboratively across the Division and the SFPUC on planning and programming efforts that strengthen public understanding of the Alameda Creek Watershed, local ecology, cultural history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. The role requires initiative, sound judgment, and a commitment to equity, public service, and environmental stewardship.

Work Schedule:
Tuesday through Saturday with occasional work on evenings and Sundays for special events, subject to change if necessary.

Working Relationship:
This position will report to the Alameda Watershed Resources Manager and will supervise a team of staff and volunteers. Initially this position will supervise the ACWC Facility Coordinator and the Education and Volunteers Coordinator, along with 6 part-time staff and several volunteers. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Nature of Work:
Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.

Essential duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategic Operations and Facility Management

Provide daily oversight of facility operations to ensure a safe, welcoming, and mission aligned visitor experience.
Lead the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures that guide facility use, visitor services, safety practices, and daily operations.
Oversee the aquarium, exhibits, grounds, and community spaces to ensure safe, high quality and consistent standards.
Direct the care, protection, and organization of collections and interpretive materials.
Oversee safety, security, and emergency preparedness efforts in alignment with SFPUC policies and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate maintenance and repairs with the facilities team and contractors, proactively identifying operational needs and improvements.

Interpretation, Education, and Program Leadership

Provide leadership for the development and delivery of interpretive, educational, and public programs that support SFPUC goals and community needs.
Establish interpretive themes related to watershed ecology, cultural and tribal history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System.
Develop program guidelines, procedures, and quality standards to ensure consistency and excellence across offerings.
Evaluate program effectiveness and develop summary reports using data and community feedback, supporting continuous improvement.
Maintain subject matter expertise in regional natural and cultural history and SFPUC systems.

Community Engagement and Partnership Development

Lead outreach, community engagement, and communications strategies that increase visibility and participation in ACWC programs.
Build and sustain partnerships with public agencies, schools, community based organizations, tribal representatives and local governments.
Represent the ACWC, the Division, and the SFPUC at public meetings, professional conferences, and community events.
Support initiatives that strengthen community relationships, advance equity, and expand access to programs and services.

Staff and Volunteer Leadership

Build and maintain staff capacity to ensure the ACWC is fully and reliably staffed for public operating hours, programs, and special events
Develop staff guidelines, volunteer protocols, and workflow procedures to support consistent operations.
Lead staff development, performance management, scheduling, and training.
Oversee volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement programs.
Provide coaching, and support to staff and volunteers, promoting a collaborative, inclusive, and service oriented culture.

Administration and Strategic Planning

Manage budgets, contracts, procurement, and HR related processes in alignment with SFPUC policies.
Develop and maintain administrative policies and procedures that support efficient, compliant, and transparent operations.
Contribute to strategic planning and the development of long term goals, policies, and operational plans for the Division and SFPUC.
Prepare reports and performance metrics that support accountability and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate And Competencies

: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here.

Role description

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC), advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. This position is responsible for overseeing the development of high quality educational and interpretive programs, and ensuring a welcoming and meaningful experience for all visitors. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position works collaboratively across the Division and the SFPUC on planning and programming efforts that strengthen public understanding of the Alameda Creek Watershed, local ecology, cultural history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. The role requires initiative, sound judgment, and a commitment to equity, public service, and environmental stewardship.

Work Schedule:
Tuesday through Saturday with occasional work on evenings and Sundays for special events, subject to change if necessary.

Working Relationship:
This position will report to the Alameda Watershed Resources Manager and will supervise a team of staff and volunteers. Initially this position will supervise the ACWC Facility Coordinator and the Education and Volunteers Coordinator, along with 6 part-time staff and several volunteers. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Nature of Work:
Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.

Essential duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategic Operations and Facility Management

Provide daily oversight of facility operations to ensure a safe, welcoming, and mission aligned visitor experience.
Lead the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures that guide facility use, visitor services, safety practices, and daily operations.
Oversee the aquarium, exhibits, grounds, and community spaces to ensure safe, high quality and consistent standards.
Direct the care, protection, and organization of collections and interpretive materials.
Oversee safety, security, and emergency preparedness efforts in alignment with SFPUC policies and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate maintenance and repairs with the facilities team and contractors, proactively identifying operational needs and improvements.

Provide leadership for the development and delivery of interpretive, educational, and public programs that support SFPUC goals and community needs.
Establish interpretive themes related to watershed ecology, cultural and tribal history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System.
Develop program guidelines, procedures, and quality standards to ensure consistency and excellence across offerings.
Evaluate program effectiveness and develop summary reports using data and community feedback, supporting continuous improvement.
Maintain subject matter expertise in regional natural and cultural history and SFPUC systems.

Community Engagement and Partnership Development

Lead outreach, community engagement, and communications strategies that increase visibility and participation in ACWC programs.
Build and sustain partnerships with public agencies, schools, community based organizations, tribal representatives and local governments.
Represent the ACWC, the Division, and the SFPUC at public meetings, professional conferences, and community events.
Support initiatives that strengthen community relationships, advance equity, and expand access to programs and services.

Lead staff development, performance management, scheduling, and training.
Oversee volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement programs.
Provide coaching, and support to staff and volunteers, promoting a collaborative, inclusive, and service oriented culture.

Manage budgets, contracts, procurement, and HR related processes in alignment with SFPUC policies.
Develop and maintain administrative policies and procedures that support efficient, compliant, and transparent operations.

Prepare reports and performance metrics that support accountability and continuous improvement.

All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

Environmental Scientist/Industrial Hygienist

Locations: Los Angeles or Orange County | ~50% field / 50% remote

Apex is seeking an environmental professional with experience in industrial hygiene to perform asbestos, lead-paint, mold/moisture intrusion, exposure assessment, abatement monitoring, and related industrial hygiene and EHS compliance projects across Southern California.

Employee Benefits

This role offers competitive compensation and a robust benefits package, a balanced mix of fieldwork and report writing, company sponsorship for professional and vocational training, work from home opportunity, collaboration with other industrial hygiene, EHS and other experts, and continued professional development and growth afforded by a rapidly growing national environmental consulting company.

Key Responsibilities

Perform asbestos, lead-based paint (LBP), and microbial/moisture intrusion assessments, along with abatement oversight, with an approximate 50/50 split between field and office work
Conduct safety and compliance assessments in accordance with regulatory standards and client requirements
Support additional environmental services through cross-training, including:
Exposure assessments
Workplace safety evaluations
Stormwater compliance inspections
Soil and groundwater sampling
Noise and air monitoring
Aboveground Storage Tank (AST) inspections

Execute work in alignment with project work plans, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and direction from project managers
Manage scheduling and logistics across all project phases, from coordination and fieldwork through reporting
Prepare clear, accurate, and technically sound client-ready reports using project-specific templates
Collaborate with internal teams to support project delivery and ongoing professional development
Maintain and proactively pursue relevant certifications, including 40-Hour HAZWOPER, CAC, and/or CSST

Qualifications

2+ years of professional experience conducting asbestos surveys and mold/moisture intrusion inspections as an AHERA-accredited inspector (in any state)
Current AHERA certification required
California Certified Asbestos Consultant (CAC) and/or Certified Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) preferred
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Microbiology, or a related field

What We’re Looking For

Self-motivated and dependable professional who can work effectively with limited supervision
Strong technical writing and critical thinking skills
Solid analytical and math skills for interpreting laboratory data and preparing reports
Excellent attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate in a team-oriented environment
Physically capable of performing fieldwork and comfortable working in both field and office settings
Commitment to safety and a strong understanding of safe work practices
Interest in growing within industrial hygiene and expanding into broader environmental consulting services

Why You'll Love Working For Us

Company-subsidized medical and dental.
Company-paid life, short, and long-term disability.
401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
Cross-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
Performance-based bonuses or other incentives.
Working with the best and brightest in the industry.
2,000+ employee national firm with 70+ locations across the US.

Our company maintains long-term, stable partnerships with many international corporations. Our work with leading technology companies continues to grow. We have successfully integrated top-tier professionals directly into their operational teams, enhancing their capabilities across multiple functions and contributing to shared success.
We are now recruiting a dedicated and detail-oriented Senior EHS Specialist to join our client’s dynamic tech environment. In this specialist role, you will be responsible for executing comprehensive EHS strategies, maintaining compliance, conducting risk assessments, and supporting the development of a strong safety mindset across all venues, including corporate offices, production facilities, and major events.

Job Description / Scope Of Work

Senior EHS Specialist
Location:
San Jose

Full-time
Job Overview

We are seeking an experienced and proactive Senior EHS Specialist to join our team. This role will be responsible for driving the implementation of EHS strategies, ensuring business operations comply with corporate policies and local regulations, fostering a strong safety culture, and enhancing employee health and safety awareness.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership:
Develop, implement, and continuously improve regional EHS strategies, policies, and procedures in alignment with corporate and business objectives.
Compliance & Risk Management:
Ensure full compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local EHS regulations. Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate EHS risks across operations.
Incident Management:
Lead and oversee incident response, investigation, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation to prevent recurrence.
Auditing & Inspection:
Plan and conduct regular EHS audits, inspections, and assessments. Track and drive closure of action items to ensure sustained compliance and safety performance.
Program Development & Training:
Design, deliver, and maintain effective EHS programs, training, and communication initiatives for employees at all levels.
Stakeholder Collaboration:
Work closely with cross-functional (XFN) teams—including Operations, HR, Facilities, and Legal—to integrate EHS into business processes and promote initiatives such as wellness, ergonomics, and employee assistance programs.
Reporting & Analysis:
Prepare and present detailed EHS performance reports, metrics, and insights to senior management and stakeholders.
Team Support & Development:
Mentor and support site-level EHS personnel and operational partners, fostering a culture of safety ownership and continuous improvement.
Business Travel:
Willingness to travel nationally and internationally as required to support regional and global business needs.

Qualifications, Skills & Experience

Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Occupational Health, or a related field. Advanced degree or professional certification (e.g., CSP, CIH, NEBOSH) is a plus.
Experience:
Minimum of 3–5 years of progressive EHS experience.
Regulatory Knowledge:
Strong working knowledge of local, state, and federal EHS regulations. Familiarity with international standards and best practices is an advantage.
Communication:
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to prepare high-quality reports and deliver effective training.
Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills:
Ability to analyze data, identify trends, and develop actionable strategies to improve EHS performance.
Technical Proficiency:
Strong computer skills, including proficiency with MS Office and EHS management systems/software.
Flexibility:
Ability to adapt to changing business needs and work outside standard hours when necessary.
Travel:
Openness to regular national as required.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in multinational or matrix organizational environments.
Demonstrated success in leading cultural change and EHS program implementation.
Knowledge of sustainability practices and wellness program integration.
